**3. manifests 仓库状态分裂（核心问题）**
报错 `revision refs/heads/master in manifests not found`。根因是 `.repo/manifests.git`（repo 实际使用的 gitdir）的 HEAD 错误地指向 `refs/heads/master`，且没有本地分支和 `[branch]` 配置，导致 repo 的 `PreSync` 无法解析出正确 revision，回退到默认的 `master`。
→ 修复：
```
git --git-dir=.repo/manifests.git update-ref refs/heads/dev-ai-contest-2026 <commit>
git --git-dir=.repo/manifests.git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/dev-ai-contest-2026
git --git-dir=.repo/manifests.git config branch.dev-ai-contest-2026.remote origin
git --git-dir=.repo/manifests.git config branch.dev-ai-contest-2026.merge refs/heads/dev-ai-contest-2026
```

############ build.sh ############
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tools/build.sh
#
# Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");

function cleanup()
{
  # keep the mapping but change to the link since:
  # 1.root can't access mount point created by normal user
  # 2.debugger could find the source code without manual setting
  fusermount -u ${MOUNTDIR}
  rmdir ${MOUNTDIR}
  ln -s ${ROOTDIR} ${MOUNTDIR}
}

function mount_unionfs()
{
  echo -e "Mount command line:"
  echo -e "  unionfs-fuse -o cow ${OUTDIR}=RW:${ROOTDIR}=RO ${MOUNTDIR}"

  rm -f ${MOUNTDIR}
  mkdir -p ${MOUNTDIR}
  unionfs-fuse -o cow ${OUTDIR}=RW:${ROOTDIR}=RO ${MOUNTDIR}
}


function build_board()
{
  echo -e "Build command line:"
  echo -e "  ${TOOLSDIR}/configure.sh -e $1"
  echo -e "  make -C ${NUTTXDIR} EXTRAFLAGS="$EXTRA_FLAGS" ${@:2}"
  echo -e "  make -C ${NUTTXDIR} savedefconfig"

  KCONFIG_ARGS="--enable-mconf --disable-nconf --disable-gconf --disable-qconf"
  if [ `uname` == "Darwin" ]; then
    KCONFIG_ARGS+=" --disable-shared --enable-static"
  fi

  if [ ! -f "${ROOTDIR}/prebuilts/kconfig-frontends/bin/kconfig-conf" ] &&
     [ ! -x "$(command -v kconfig-conf)" ]; then
    pushd ${ROOTDIR}/prebuilts/kconfig-frontends
    ./configure --prefix=${ROOTDIR}/prebuilts/kconfig-frontends ${KCONFIG_ARGS} 1>/dev/null
    touch aclocal.m4 Makefile.in
    make install 1>/dev/null
    popd
  fi
  export PATH=${ROOTDIR}/prebuilts/kconfig-frontends/bin:$PATH

  if ! ${TOOLSDIR}/configure.sh -e $1; then
    echo "Error: ############# config ${1} fail ##############"
    exit 1
  fi

  if [[ ${CUSTOM_COMPILER} == "tasking" ]]; then
    kconfig-tweak --file ${NUTTXDIR}/.config --enable CONFIG_TRICORE_TOOLCHAIN_TASKING
  fi

  GHS_OPTS_STRING="CONFIG_ARCH_TOOLCHAIN_GHS=y"
  TASKING_OPTS_STRING="CONFIG_TRICORE_TOOLCHAIN_TASKING=y"
  if grep -qE "^(${GHS_OPTS_STRING}|${TASKING_OPTS_STRING})$" "${NUTTXDIR}/.config"; then
    echo "EXTRA_FLAGS are required to update the when using the GHS or Tasking toolchain."
    EXTRA_FLAGS=$(echo "$EXTRA_FLAGS" | sed 's/-Wno-cpp//' | xargs)
  fi

  if ! ${BEAR} make -C ${NUTTXDIR} EXTRAFLAGS="$EXTRA_FLAGS" ${@:2}; then
    echo "Error: ############# build ${1} fail ##############"
    exit 2
  else
    if [ -f "${COMPILE_COMMANDS}" ]; then
      cp ${COMPILE_COMMANDS} ${COMPILE_COMMANDS_BACKUP}
    fi
  fi

  if echo "${@:2}" | grep -q "distclean"; then
    if [ -f "${COMPILE_COMMANDS}" ]; then
      rm -rf ${COMPILE_COMMANDS}
    fi
    return;
  fi

  if ! make -C ${NUTTXDIR} savedefconfig; then
    echo "Error: ############# save ${1} fail ##############"
    exit 3
  fi

  if [ ! -d $1 ]; then
    cp ${NUTTXDIR}/defconfig ${ROOTDIR}/nuttx/boards/*/*/${1/[:|\/]//configs/}
  else
    if grep -q "#include" "$1/defconfig"; then
      echo "Note: skipping savedefconfig for debug defconfig."
    else
      cp ${NUTTXDIR}/defconfig $1
    fi
  fi
}

function build_board_cmake()
{
  # first check if the command target is `distclean`
  # cmake is built for out-of-tree, so delete the CMAKE_BINARY_DIR directory directly
  if echo "${@:2}" | grep -q "distclean"; then
    echo -e "Build target distclean:"
    echo -e "  there is no need to distclean in cmake, delete '${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}' directly"
    if [ -d "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}" ]; then
      rm -rf $CMAKE_BINARY_DIR
    fi
    return 0
  fi
  # check parallelism
  j_arg=$(echo ${@:2} |grep -oP '\-j[0-9]+')
  # cmake verbose
  v_arg=""

  # remove the -Wno-cpp build option from ghs build options
  GHS_OPTS_STRING="CONFIG_ARM_TOOLCHAIN_GHS=y"
  TASKING_OPTS_STRING="CONFIG_TRICORE_TOOLCHAIN_TASKING=y"
  defconfig_path=$1/defconfig
  valid_defconfig_path=$(echo ${defconfig_path} | sed 's/^.\{3\}//')
  if grep -qE "^(${GHS_OPTS_STRING}|${TASKING_OPTS_STRING})$" "${valid_defconfig_path}"; then
    echo "EXTRA_FLAGS are required to update the when using the GHS toolchain."
    EXTRA_FLAGS=$(echo "$EXTRA_FLAGS" | sed 's/-Wno-cpp//' | xargs)
  fi
  export VELA_EXTRA_FLAGS="$EXTRA_FLAGS"
  # let use lunch directily
  echo " lunch $1 ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR} "
  lunch $1 ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}
  echo
  # check if the command target is `Xconfig`
  for arg in "${@:2}"
  do
    if [[ $arg == *config ]]; then
      if ! m $arg; then
        echo "Error: #############  m $arg fail ##############"
        exit 2
      else
        return 0
      fi
    fi
    if [[ "$arg" =~ ^V=1$ ]]; then
      v_arg+="V=1"
    fi
  done
  # do cmake build
  if ! m $j_arg $v_arg; then
    echo "Error: ############# build ${1} fail ##############"
    exit 2
  fi
}


function setup_cmake_binary_dir()
{
  local boardconfig=$1
  if [ -d ${ROOTDIR}/${boardconfig} ]; then
    # parse path config
    config_name=$(basename "$boardconfig")
    board_name=$(basename $(dirname $(dirname "$boardconfig")))
  else
    # parse nuttx config pair
    config_name=`echo ${boardconfig} | cut -s -d':' -f2`
    if [ -z "${config_name}" ]; then
      board_name=`echo ${boardconfig} | cut -d'/' -f1`
      config_name=`echo ${boardconfig} | cut -d'/' -f2`
    else
      board_name=`echo ${boardconfig} | cut -d':' -f1`
    fi
  fi
  CMAKE_BINARY_DIR+="/${board_name}_${config_name}"
}

if [ $# == 0 ]; then
  echo "Usage: $0 [-m] <board-name>:<config-name> [-e <extraflags>] [--cmake] [-b <cmake_binary_dir>] [--dis-ninja] [make options]"
  echo ""
  echo "Where:"
  echo "  -m: out of tree build. Or default in tree build without it."
  echo "  -e: pass extra c/c++ flags such as -Werror via make command line"
  echo "  --cmake: switch the build mode to CMake compilation."
  echo "  -b: set custom binary directory for CMake."
  echo "  --dis-ninja: disable CMake Ninja generator fo default."
  echo "  -c: set custom toolchain."
  exit 1
fi

ROOTDIR=$(dirname $(readlink -f ${0}))
ROOTDIR=$(realpath ${ROOTDIR}/../..)

CONFIGPATH=$2

if [ $1 == "-m" ]; then
  # out of tree build
  confparams=(${CONFIGPATH//:/ })
  configdir=${confparams[1]}

  if [ -z "${configdir}" ]; then
    # handle cases where the end is a "/"
    if [ "${CONFIGPATH:(-1)}" = "/" ]; then
      CONFIGPATH=${CONFIGPATH:0:-1}
    fi
    boarddir=`echo ${CONFIGPATH} | rev | cut -d'/' -f3 | rev`
    configdir=`echo ${CONFIGPATH} | rev | cut -d'/' -f1 | rev`
  else
    boarddir=${confparams[0]}
  fi

  OUTDIR=${ROOTDIR}/out/${boarddir}/${configdir}
  MOUNTDIR=${OUTDIR}/.unionfs
  NUTTXDIR=${MOUNTDIR}/nuttx

  trap cleanup EXIT
  mount_unionfs
  shift
else
  # in tree build
  OUTDIR=${ROOTDIR}
  NUTTXDIR=${ROOTDIR}/nuttx
fi

TOOLSDIR=${NUTTXDIR}/tools
board_config=$1
shift

source ${ROOTDIR}/build/envsetup.sh

EXTRA_FLAGS="-Wno-cpp -Wno-deprecated-declarations"
while [[ "$1" == "-e" ]]; do
  shift
  EXTRA_FLAGS+=" $1"
  echo "extraflags: $EXTRA_FLAGS"
  shift
done

if [ "$1" == "--cmake" ]; then
  CMAKE_BINARY_DIR="cmake_out"
  CMAKE_GENERATOR="-GNinja"
  CMAKE_BUILD="cmake"
  setup_cmake_binary_dir $board_config
  shift
fi

if [ "$1" == "-b" ]; then
  shift
  CMAKE_BINARY_DIR="$1"
  echo "custom CMake binary dir: $CMAKE_BINARY_DIR"
  shift
fi

if [ "$1" == "--dis-ninja" ]; then
  CMAKE_GENERATOR=""
  shift
fi

if [ "$1" == "-c" ]; then
  shift
  CUSTOM_COMPILER="$1"
  echo "custom toolchain: $CUSTOM_COMPILER"
  shift
fi

# Determine the config path
if [ -d ${ROOTDIR}/${board_config} ]; then
  config_path="${ROOTDIR}/${board_config}"
else
  config_path="${board_config}"
fi

# Build with appropriate method
if [ -z "$CMAKE_BUILD" ]; then
  build_board ${config_path} $*
else
  build_board_cmake ${board_config} $*
fi


############ emulator.sh ############
#!/bin/bash

if [ x"$(uname)" == x"Linux" ]; then
  HOST_OS="linux"
elif [ x"$(uname)" == x"Darwin" ]; then
  HOST_OS="darwin"
fi

if [ x"$(uname -m)" == x"arm64" -o x"$(uname -m)" == x"aarch64" ]; then
  HOST_ARCH="aarch64"
elif [ x"$(uname -m)" == x"x86_64" ]; then
  HOST_ARCH="x86_64"
fi

if [ x"$(uname)" == x"Darwin" ]; then
TOP_DIR=$(realpath $0 | sed 's#/prebuilts/emulator/tools/emulator.sh##g')
else
TOP_DIR=$(readlink -f $0 | sed 's#/prebuilts/emulator/tools/emulator.sh##g')
fi

EMULATOR_DIR="${TOP_DIR}/prebuilts/emulator/${HOST_OS}-${HOST_ARCH}"
EMULATOR_BIN="${EMULATOR_DIR}/emulator"

usage()
{
  echo "Usage:"
  echo "Run Emulator with out-of-tree artifacts:"
  echo "  Example: $0 cmake_out/vela_qemu-arm64-v8a-ap"
  echo "Run Emulator with board name [deprecated]:"
  echo "  Example: $0 vela"
  exit 1
}

merge_args()
{
  EMULATOR_GOLDFISH_ARGS=""
  EMULATOR_QEMU_ARGS=""

  found_qemu=false
  for arg in ${EMULATOR_COMMON_ARGS}; do
    if [ "${arg}" == "-qemu" ]; then
        found_qemu=true
        continue
    fi

    if ${found_qemu}; then
        EMULATOR_QEMU_ARGS="$EMULATOR_QEMU_ARGS $arg"
    else
        EMULATOR_GOLDFISH_ARGS="$EMULATOR_GOLDFISH_ARGS $arg"
    fi
  done

  found_qemu=false
  for arg in ${EMULATOR_EXTRA_ARGS}; do
    if [ "${arg}" == "-qemu" ]; then
        found_qemu=true
        continue
    fi

    if ${found_qemu}; then
        EMULATOR_QEMU_ARGS="$EMULATOR_QEMU_ARGS $arg"
    else
        EMULATOR_GOLDFISH_ARGS="$EMULATOR_GOLDFISH_ARGS $arg"
    fi
  done

  echo ${EMULATOR_GOLDFISH_ARGS} -qemu ${EMULATOR_QEMU_ARGS}
}

# for out-of-tree artifacts
if test -e "$1/.config"; then
  OUT_DIR="$1"
  shift
  if grep -q '^CONFIG_ARCH_ARM=y' ${OUT_DIR}/.config; then
    QEMU_ARCH="arm"
  elif grep -q '^CONFIG_ARCH_ARM64=y' ${OUT_DIR}/.config; then
    QEMU_ARCH="aarch64"
  elif grep -q '^CONFIG_ARCH_X86=y' ${OUT_DIR}/.config; then
    QEMU_ARCH="i386"
  elif grep -q '^CONFIG_ARCH_X86_64=y' ${OUT_DIR}/.config; then
    QEMU_ARCH="x86_64"
  elif grep -q '^CONFIG_ARCH_RISCV=y' ${OUT_DIR}/.config; then
    QEMU_ARCH="riscv32"
  fi
  if grep -q '^CONFIG_ARCH_CHIP_QEMU=y' ${OUT_DIR}/.config; then
    EMULATOR_DIR="${TOP_DIR}/prebuilts/qemu/${HOST_OS}-${HOST_ARCH}"
    EMULATOR_BIN="${EMULATOR_DIR}/bin/qemu-system-${QEMU_ARCH}"
    EMULATOR_ARGS="-L ${EMULATOR_DIR}/share/qemu -kernel ${OUT_DIR}/nuttx $(cat ${OUT_DIR}/qemu_args.txt)"
    echo "RUN ${EMULATOR_BIN} ${EMULATOR_ARGS}"
    ${EMULATOR_BIN} ${EMULATOR_ARGS}
  elif grep -Eq '^CONFIG_ARCH_CHIP_GOLDFISH_(ARM|ARM64|X86_64)=y' ${OUT_DIR}/.config; then
    mkdir -p ${OUT_DIR}/system
    echo "ro.product.cpu.abi=${QEMU_ARCH}" | sed 's/aarch64/arm64/g' > ${OUT_DIR}/system/build.prop
    export ANDROID_EMULATOR_VELA=true
    export ANDROID_BUILD_TOP=${TOP_DIR}
    export ANDROID_PRODUCT_OUT=${OUT_DIR}
    export EMULATOR_COMMON_ARGS="-show-kernel -verbose"
    if [[ "${QEMU_ARCH}" = "x86"* ]]; then
      EMULATOR_COMMON_ARGS="${EMULATOR_COMMON_ARGS} -qemu -cpu Skylake-Client,-hle,-rtm,-mpx"
    else
      EMULATOR_COMMON_ARGS="${EMULATOR_COMMON_ARGS} -qemu -device virtio-snd,bus=virtio-mmio-bus.2 -allow-host-audio"
    fi
    EMULATOR_EXTRA_ARGS="$@"
    EMULATOR_MERGED_ARGS=$(merge_args ${EMULATOR_COMMON_ARGS} ${EMULATOR_EXTRA_ARGS})
    echo "RUN ${EMULATOR_BIN} ${EMULATOR_MERGED_ARGS}"
    ${EMULATOR_BIN} ${EMULATOR_MERGED_ARGS}
  fi
# for deprecated method
else
  if test -n "$1"; then
    BOARD_NAME=$1
  else
    usage
  fi

  if test -d ${TOP_DIR}/vendor/qemu/boards/${BOARD_NAME}; then
    TARGETDIR=${TOP_DIR}/vendor/qemu/boards/${BOARD_NAME}
  elif test -d ${TOP_DIR}/vendor/openvela/boards/${BOARD_NAME}; then
    TARGETDIR=${TOP_DIR}/vendor/openvela/boards/${BOARD_NAME}
  else
    usage
  fi

  echo "TARGETDIR = ${TARGETDIR}"
  shift

  source ${TARGETDIR}/prebuilts/tools/run_emulator.sh
fi

# reset environment
deactivate() {
    # reset path
    if [ -n "${VELA_ORIGINAL_PATH:-}" ]; then
        PATH="${VELA_ORIGINAL_PATH:-}"
        export PATH
        unset VELA_ORIGINAL_PATH
    fi
    # rset prompt
    if [ -n "${VELA_ORIGINAL_PS1:-}" ]; then
        PS1="${VELA_ORIGINAL_PS1:-}"
        export PS1
        unset VELA_ORIGINAL_PS1
    fi
    # reset build variables
    unset VELA_BUILD_TARGET_VENDOR
    unset VELA_BUILD_TARGET_BOARD
    unset VELA_BUILD_TARGET_CONFIG
    unset VELA_BUILD_BOARD_CONFIG
    unset VELA_EXTRA_FLAGS
    unset VELA_CMAKE_GENERATOR
    unset VELA_USE_MAKEFILE

    # reset CCACHE strategy
    unset CCACHE_BASEDIR
    unset CCACHE_COMPILERCHECK
    unset CCACHE_NOHASHDIR
    unset CCACHE_SLOPPINESS
    if [ ! "${1:-}" = "nondestructive" ]; then
        # reset nuttx custom name null
        if [[ "${NUTTX_DIR_NAME}" == "nuttx" ]]; then
            unset NUTTX_DIR_NAME
        fi
        # Self destruct!
        unset -f deactivate
    fi
}

# Help prompt

162	    lines=($(\grep "$1" $FILELIST | sed -e 's/\/[^/]*$//' | sort | uniq))
163	    if [[ ${#lines[@]} = 0 ]]; then
164	        echo "Not found"
165	        return
166	    fi
167	    local pathname
168	    local choice
169	    if [[ ${#lines[@]} > 1 ]]; then
170	        while [[ -z "$pathname" ]]; do
171	            local index=1
172	            local line
173	            for line in ${lines[@]}; do
174	                printf "%6s %s\n" "[$index]" $line
175	                index=$(($index + 1))
176	            done
177	            echo
178	            echo -n "Select one: "
179	            unset choice
180	            read choice
181	            if [[ $choice -gt ${#lines[@]} || $choice -lt 1 ]]; then
182	                echo "Invalid choice"
183	                continue
184	            fi
185	            pathname=${lines[@]:$(($choice - 1)):1}
186	        done
187	    else
188	        pathname=${lines[@]:0:1}
189	    fi
190	    \cd $T/$pathname
191	}

280	# Function: dump_build_choices
281	# Description:
282	#   This function searches for build choices within a vendor directory structure.
283	#   It identifies directories that contain a 'boards' subdirectory and further
284	#   filters those boards directories to find subdirectories with a 'configs'
285	#   subdirectory and a 'CMakeLists.txt' file. The function then constructs a
286	#   formatted string for each matching configuration and prints the results.
287	#
288	# Usage:
289	#   dump_build_choices
290	#
291	# Output:
292	#   Prints a list of formatted strings, each representing a build choice in the
293	#   format '[vendor_dir]-[board_dir]-[config_dir]', where:
294	#     - vendor_dir is the name of the directory containing 'boards'.
295	#     - board_dir is the name of the 'boards' subdirectory.
296	#     - config_dir is the name of the 'configs' subdirectory.
297	#
298	# Example:
299	#   If the structure is as follows:
300	#   vendor/bouffalolab/boards/bl616evb/configs/nsh
301	#   The output might be:
302	#   [bouffalolab]-[bl616evb]-[nsh]
303	#
304	# Note:
305	#   This function assumes that the 'gettop' function is defined and returns the
306	#   root directory of the project. It also assumes that the 'boards' and 'configs'
307	#   directories, as well as the 'CMakeLists.txt' file, are present in the expected
308	#   locations.
309	#
310	function dump_build_choices() {
311	    # Define the starting directory as the 'vendor' directory within the project root.
312	    start_dir=$(gettop)/vendor
313	
314	    # Initialize an array to hold directories containing 'boards'.
315	    list_of_dirs=()
316	
317	    # Search for directories at the first level under 'start_dir' that contain 'boards'.
318	    find "$start_dir" -maxdepth 1 -type d | while read -r dir; do
319	        if [[ -d "${dir}/boards" ]]; then
320	            # If a 'boards' directory is found, add the parent directory to the list.
321	            list_of_dirs+=("$dir")
322	        fi
323	    done
324	
325	    # Initialize an array to hold the final formatted results.
326	    final_results=()
327	
328	    # Iterate over each directory in the list that contains 'boards'.
329	    for parent_dir in "${list_of_dirs[@]}"; do
330	        # Search for subdirectories within the 'boards' directory.
331	        find "$parent_dir/boards" -maxdepth 1 -type d ! -path "$parent_dir/boards" | while read -r subdir; do
332	            # Check if the subdirectory contains 'configs' and a 'CMakeLists.txt' file.
333	            if [[ -d "${subdir}/configs" && -f "${subdir}/CMakeLists.txt" ]]; then
334	                # Get all subdirectories within 'configs'.
335	                configs_subdirs=("$subdir"/configs/*)
336	                for config_subdir in "${configs_subdirs[@]}"; do
337	                    if [[ -d "$config_subdir" ]]; then
338	                        # Format the result string and add it to the final results array.
339	                        final_results+=("[$(basename $parent_dir)]-[$(basename $subdir)]-[$(basename $config_subdir)]")
340	                    fi
341	                done
342	            fi
343	            # boards chip level config such as bes
344	            find $subdir -maxdepth 1 -type d ! -path $subdir | while read -r chipdir; do
345	                if [[ -d "${chipdir}/configs" && -f "${chipdir}/CMakeLists.txt" ]]; then
346	                    # Get all subdirectories within 'configs'.
347	                    configs_subdirs=("$chipdir"/configs/*)
348	                    for config_subdir in "${configs_subdirs[@]}"; do
349	                        if [[ -d "$config_subdir" ]]; then
350	                            # Format the result string and add it to the final results array.
351	                            final_results+=("[$(basename $parent_dir)]-[$(basename $chipdir)]-[$(basename $config_subdir)]")
352	                        fi
353	                    done
354	                fi
355	            done
356	        done
357	    done
358	    # Print the final results.
359	    printf '%s\n' "${final_results[@]}"
360	}

437	function lunch() {
438	    # sanity checks
439	    if [[ $# -gt 2 ]]; then
440	        echo "usage: lunch [target] [outdir]" >&2
441	        return 1
442	    fi
443	    local TOP_DIR=$(gettop)
444	    local config_name
445	    local board_name
446	    local vendor_name
447	    local boardconfig
448	    local lunch_with_specific_config
449	    # lunch specific args
450	    if [[ $# -ge 1 ]] && ! [[ "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
451	        boardconfig=$1
452	        # 1.lunch with full path config
453	        if [ -d "$TOP_DIR/$boardconfig" ]; then
454	            config_name=$(basename "$boardconfig")
455	            board_name=$(basename $(dirname $(dirname "$boardconfig")))
456	            if [[ $boardconfig =~ ^(\./)?vendor/ ]]; then
457	                vendor_name=$(echo "${boardconfig#./}" | cut -d'/' -f2)
458	            else
459	                vendor_name=$NUTTX_DIR_NAME
460	            fi
461	            boardconfig="../$boardconfig"
462	        # 2.lunch with nuttx config pair
463	        else
464	            config_name=$(echo ${boardconfig} | cut -s -d':' -f2)
465	            if [ -z "${config_name}" ]; then
466	                board_name=$(echo ${boardconfig} | cut -d'/' -f1)
467	                config_name=$(echo ${boardconfig} | cut -d'/' -f2)
468	            else
469	                board_name=$(echo ${boardconfig} | cut -d':' -f1)
470	            fi
471	            vendor_name=$NUTTX_DIR_NAME
472	        fi
473	
474	        lunch_with_specific_config=true
475	
476	    fi
477	
478	    if [[ "$lunch_with_specific_config" != "true" ]]; then
479	        local answer
480	
481	        local used_lunch_menu=0
482	
483	        if [ "$1" ]; then
484	            answer=$1
485	        else
486	            print_lunch_menu
487	            echo "Which would you like?"
488	            echo -n "Pick from common choices above or specify your own: "
489	            read answer
490	            used_lunch_menu=1
491	        fi
492	
493	        local selection=
494	        if [ -z "$answer" ]; then
495	            selection="[sim]-[vela]-[vela]"
496	        elif (echo -n $answer | grep -q -e "^[0-9][0-9]*$"); then
497	            local -a choices=()
498	            while IFS= read -r line; do
499	                choices+=("$line")
500	            done < <(dump_vendor_choices)
501	            if [ $answer -le ${#choices[@]} ]; then
502	                # array in zsh starts from 1 instead of 0.
503	                if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
504	                    selection=${choices[$(($answer))]}
505	                else
506	                    selection=${choices[$(($answer - 1))]}
507	                fi
508	            fi
509	        else
510	            selection=$answer
511	        fi
512	
513	        export TARGET_BUILD_APPS=
514	
515	        # This must be [vendor]-[board]-[config]
516	        split_selection="${selection:1:${#selection}-2}"
517	        split_selection=$(echo "$split_selection" | sed 's/]-\[/,/g')
518	        IFS="," read -r vendor_name board_name config_name <<<"$split_selection"
519	        if [[ -z "$vendor_name" ]] || [[ -z "$board_name" ]] || [[ -z "$config_name" ]]; then
520	            echo
521	            echo "Invalid lunch combo: $selection"
522	            echo "Valid combos must be of the form [vendor]-[board]-[config]"
523	            return 1
524	        fi
525	
526	    fi
527	
528	    # clean first
529	    clean_select_configs
530	    export VELA_BUILD_TARGET_VENDOR=$vendor_name
531	    export VELA_BUILD_TARGET_BOARD=$board_name
532	    export VELA_BUILD_TARGET_CONFIG=$config_name
533	    export VELA_BUILD_BOARD_CONFIG=$boardconfig
534	
535	    echo -e "The current build configuration lunched with: \033[32m[$vendor_name]-[$board_name]-[$config_name]!\033[0m"
536	    echo
537	    if _is_makefile "[$vendor_name]-[$board_name]-[$config_name]"; then
538	        echo -e "\033[33m[$vendor_name]-[$board_name]-[$config_name] config remain in makefile.\033[0m"
539	        return 0
540	    fi
541	
542	    # lunch with custom binary dir
543	    if [ -n "${2:-}" ]; then
544	        if [[ "$2" =~ ^/ ]]; then
545	                export CURRENT_LUNCH_BINARY_DIR=$2
546	        else
547	            export CURRENT_LUNCH_BINARY_DIR=${TOP_DIR}/$2
548	        fi
549	    else
550	        export CURRENT_LUNCH_BINARY_DIR=${TOP_DIR}/out/${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_VENDOR}_${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_BOARD}_${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_CONFIG}
551	    fi
552	
553	    echo -e "\033[32m#### BINARY directory is set: ${CURRENT_LUNCH_BINARY_DIR}\033[0m"
554	}

556	function _wrap_build() {
557	    TOP_DIR=$(gettop)
558	    OUT_DIR=$TOP_DIR/out
559	    NUTTXDIR=$TOP_DIR/$NUTTX_DIR_NAME
560	    CMAKE_BINARY_DIR=$CURRENT_LUNCH_BINARY_DIR
561	
562	    if [ -z "${VELA_BUILD_BOARD_CONFIG}" ]; then
563	        if [ -d "$TOP_DIR/vendor/${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_VENDOR}/boards/${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_BOARD}/configs/${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_CONFIG}" ]; then
564	            BOARD_CONFIG="../vendor/${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_VENDOR}/boards/${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_BOARD}/configs/${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_CONFIG}"
565	        else
566	            BOARD_CONFIG="../$(dirname vendor/${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_VENDOR}/boards/*/${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_BOARD}/configs/${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_CONFIG})/${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_CONFIG}"
567	        fi
568	    else
569	        BOARD_CONFIG=${VELA_BUILD_BOARD_CONFIG}
570	    fi
571	
572	    # vendor hook before the actual build
573	    local triple_config_meta="[$VELA_BUILD_TARGET_VENDOR]-[$VELA_BUILD_TARGET_BOARD]-[$VELA_BUILD_TARGET_CONFIG]"
574	    if _has_vendor_hook $triple_config_meta; then
575	        echo " execute the vendor hook function for $triple_config_meta:"
576	        "${VENDOR_PRE_BUILD_HOOK_MAP[$triple_config_meta]}" $BOARD_CONFIG
577	    fi
578	
579	    if [[ "${VELA_QUIET_BUILD:-}" == true ]]; then
580	        "$@"
581	        return $?
582	    fi
583	    local start_time=$(date +"%s")
584	    "$@"
585	    local ret=$?
586	    local end_time=$(date +"%s")
587	    local tdiff=$(($end_time - $start_time))
588	    local hours=$(($tdiff / 3600))
589	    local mins=$((($tdiff % 3600) / 60))
590	    local secs=$(($tdiff % 60))
591	    local ncolors=$(tput colors 2>/dev/null)
592	    if [ -n "$ncolors" ] && [ $ncolors -ge 8 ]; then
593	        color_failed=$'\E'"[0;31m"
594	        color_success=$'\E'"[0;32m"
595	        color_warning=$'\E'"[0;33m"
596	        color_reset=$'\E'"[00m"
597	    else
598	        color_failed=""
599	        color_success=""
600	        color_reset=""
601	    fi
602	
603	    echo
604	    if [ $ret -eq 0 ]; then
605	        echo -n "${color_success}#### build completed successfully "
606	    else
607	        echo -n "${color_failed}#### failed to build some targets "
608	    fi
609	    if [ $hours -gt 0 ]; then
610	        printf "(%02g:%02g:%02g (hh:mm:ss))" $hours $mins $secs
611	    elif [ $mins -gt 0 ]; then
612	        printf "(%02g:%02g (mm:ss))" $mins $secs
613	    elif [ $secs -gt 0 ]; then
614	        printf "(%s seconds)" $secs
615	    fi
616	    echo " ####${color_reset}"
617	
618	    return $ret
619	}

621	function _trigger_build() (
622	    # have we already lunched ?
623	    if [ -z "${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_CONFIG}" ]; then
624	        echo "No BUILD TARGET found, please lunch first: lunch [target]"
625	        exit 1
626	    fi

628	    shift
629	    local T=$(gettop)
630	    if [ -n "$T" ]; then
631	        _wrap_build ${bc} "$@"
632	    else
633	        echo >&2 "Couldn't locate the top of the tree. Try setting TOP."
634	        return 1
635	    fi
636	    local ret=$?
637	    return $ret
638	)

652	function get_make_command() {
653	    # If we're in the Makefile directory, use the real make
654	    if [ -f Makefile ]; then
655	        echo command make
656	        return
657	    fi
658	    # Always use the real make if -C is passed in
659	    for arg in "$@"; do
660	        if [[ $arg == -C* ]]; then
661	            echo command make
662	            return
663	        fi
664	    done
665	    echo m
666	}

672	function _do_cmake_generator() {
673	    if command -v ccache &> /dev/null; then
674	        VELA_CMAKE_USE_CCACHE=ccache
675	    fi
676	    if [ ! -d "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}" ]; then
677	        local T=$(gettop)
678	        echo -e "Build CMake configuration:"
679	        echo -e "  cmake -B ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR} -S ${NUTTXDIR} -DBOARD_CONFIG=${BOARD_CONFIG} -DCUSTOM_MODULE_PATH="$T/build/cmake" -DEXTRA_FLAGS=\"${VELA_EXTRA_FLAGS}\" ${VELA_CMAKE_GENERATOR}"
680	        if ! cmake -B ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR} -S ${NUTTXDIR} -DBOARD_CONFIG=${BOARD_CONFIG} -DCUSTOM_MODULE_PATH="$T/build/cmake" -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=${VELA_CMAKE_USE_CCACHE} -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=${VELA_CMAKE_USE_CCACHE} -DEXTRA_FLAGS="${VELA_EXTRA_FLAGS}" ${VELA_CMAKE_GENERATOR}; then
681	            echo "Error: ############# config ${1} fail ##############"
682	            exit 1
683	        fi
684	    fi
685	}

687	# FIXME:
688	# This function is used to build the Makefile project.
689	# Used as a transitional tool for projects that do not yet support the full CMake build configuration
690	function _do_makefile_build() {
691	    echo "Note: execute build for Makefile."
692	    echo -e "Build command line:"
693	    echo -e "  ${TOOLSDIR}/configure.sh -e $T/nuttx/${BOARD_CONFIG}"
694	    echo -e "  make -C ${NUTTXDIR} EXTRAFLAGS="$VELA_EXTRA_FLAGS" ${@}"
695	    echo -e "  make -C ${NUTTXDIR} savedefconfig"
696	    local T=$(gettop)
697	    local NUTTXDIR=${T}/nuttx
698	    local TOOLSDIR=${NUTTXDIR}/tools
699	    local lunched="[$VELA_BUILD_TARGET_VENDOR]-[$VELA_BUILD_TARGET_BOARD]-[$VELA_BUILD_TARGET_CONFIG]"
700	    local fixed_config=$(cat "$T/.vela_makefile_fixed_config" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
701	    local j_arg=$(echo ${@} | grep -oE '\-j[0-9]+')
702	    if [ -z "$j_arg" ]; then
703	        j_arg="-j$(_get_recommended_jobs)"
704	    fi
705	    if [[ -n "$fixed_config" && "$lunched" != "$fixed_config" ]]; then
706	        echo "\033[33mcurrent lunched has changed from $fixed_config to $lunched \033[0m"
707	        if [ -f $T/nuttx/.config ]; then
708	            echo "\033[33m do make distclean first: \033[0m"
709	            make -C ${NUTTXDIR} distclean $j_arg
710	        fi
711	    fi
712	    if [ ! -r $T/nuttx/.config ]; then
713	        if ! ${TOOLSDIR}/configure.sh -e $T/nuttx/${BOARD_CONFIG}; then
714	            echo "Error: ############# config $T/nuttx/${BOARD_CONFIG} fail ##############"
715	            exit 1
716	        fi
717	        echo $lunched > $T/.vela_makefile_fixed_config
718	    fi
719	
720	    if command -v ccache &> /dev/null; then
721	        VELA_MAKEFILE_USE_CCACHE="CCACHE=ccache"
722	    fi
723	
724	    if ! makefile_bear make -C ${NUTTXDIR} EXTRAFLAGS="$VELA_EXTRA_FLAGS" $VELA_MAKEFILE_USE_CCACHE ${@} $j_arg; then
725	        echo "Error: ############# build $T/nuttx/${BOARD_CONFIG} fail ##############"
726	        exit 2
727	    fi
728	
729	    if echo "${@}" | grep -q "distclean"; then
730	        return
731	    fi
732	
733	    if ! make -C ${NUTTXDIR} savedefconfig; then
734	        echo "Error: ############# save $T/nuttx/${BOARD_CONFIG} fail ##############"
735	        exit 3
736	    else
737	        if echo "${@}" | grep -q "savedefconfig"; then
738	            if [ -d $T/nuttx/${BOARD_CONFIG} ]; then
739	                if grep -q "#include" "$T/nuttx/${BOARD_CONFIG}/defconfig"; then
740	                    echo "Note: skipping savedefconfig for debug defconfig."
741	                else
742	                    cp ${NUTTXDIR}/defconfig $T/nuttx/${BOARD_CONFIG}
743	                fi
744	            fi
745	        fi
746	    fi
747	}

749	function _build_board() {
750	
751	    # check if remain Makefile
752	    if _is_makefile "[${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_VENDOR}]-[${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_BOARD}]-[${VELA_BUILD_TARGET_CONFIG}]"  || [ "${VELA_USE_MAKEFILE}" = "1" ]; then
753	        _do_makefile_build "$@"
754	        return 0
755	    fi
756	
757	    # first check if the command target is `distclean`
758	    # cmake is built for out-of-tree, so delete the CMAKE_BINARY_DIR directory directly
759	    if echo "${@:1}" | grep -q "clean"; then
760	        echo -e "Build target distclean:"
761	        echo -e "  there is no need to distclean in cmake, delete '${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}' directly"
762	        if [ -d "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}" ]; then
763	            rm -rf $CMAKE_BINARY_DIR
764	        fi
765	        return 0
766	    fi
767	    # check parallelism
768	    j_arg=$(echo ${@:1} | grep -oE '\-j[0-9]+')
769	    if [ -z "$j_arg" ]; then
770	        j_arg="-j$(_get_recommended_jobs)"
771	    fi
772	    # cmake verbose
773	    v_arg=""
774	    # ninja args
775	    ninja_arg=("--")
776	
777	    # convenient way to enable extra flags
778	    local extra_flags_str=""
779	    local found_extra_flags=0
780	    for arg in "${@:1}"; do
781	        if [[ "$found_extra_flags" == "1" ]]; then
782	            extra_flags_str="$extra_flags_str $arg"
783	            found_extra_flags=0
784	        elif [[ "$arg" == "-e" ]]; then
785	            found_extra_flags=1
786	        fi
787	    done
788	
789	    if [ ! -z "$extra_flags_str" ]; then
790	        echo -e "use custom extra flags: $extra_flags_str"
791	        export VELA_EXTRA_FLAGS="$VELA_EXTRA_FLAGS $extra_flags_str"
792	    fi
793	
794	    # check if cmake configuration is required
795	    _do_cmake_generator
796	    # check if the command target is `Xconfig`
797	    for arg in "${@:1}"; do
798	        if [[ $arg == *config ]]; then
799	            echo -e "  cmake --build ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR} -t $arg"
800	            if ! cmake --build ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR} -t $arg; then
801	                echo "Error: ############# CMake -t $arg fail ##############"
802	                exit 2
803	            else
804	                return 0
805	            fi
806	        fi
807	        if [[ "$arg" =~ ^V=1$ ]]; then
808	            v_arg+="-v"
809	        fi
810	        if [[ "$arg" =~ ^--keeprsp$ ]]; then
811	            ninja_arg+=("-d")
812	            ninja_arg+=("keeprsp")
813	        fi
814	        if [[ "$arg" =~ ^--keepdep$ ]]; then
815	            ninja_arg+=("-d")
816	            ninja_arg+=("keepdepfile")
817	        fi
818	        if [[ "$arg" =~ ^--keepgoing$ ]]; then
819	            ninja_arg+=("-k")
820	            ninja_arg+=("0")
821	        fi
822	    done
823	    # do cmake build
824	    echo -e "  cmake --build ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR} $j_arg $v_arg ${ninja_arg[@]}"
825	    if ! cmake --build ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR} $j_arg $v_arg ${ninja_arg[@]}; then
826	        echo "Error: ############# build ${1} fail ##############"
827	        exit 2
828	    fi
829	    # do cmake install
830	    if [[ ! -z $CMAKE_WITH_INSTALL ]]; then
831	        echo -e "  cmake --install ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}"
832	        if ! cmake --install ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}; then
833	            echo "Error: ############# CMake install fail ##############"
834	            exit 2
835	        else
836	            return 0
837	        fi
838	    fi
839	
840	}

856	function _build_current_target() {
857	    local T=$(gettop)
858	    # first check whether CMake generator is done
859	    _do_cmake_generator
860	    # where we should find in CMake BINAR dir?
861	    if [[ "$PWD" == "$T/$NUTTX_DIR_NAME"* ]]; then
862	        relative_path=$(realpath -s --relative-to="$T/$NUTTX_DIR_NAME" "$PWD")
863	    else
864	        relative_path=$(realpath -s --relative-to="$T" "$PWD")
865	    fi
866	    target_path=${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/${relative_path}
867	    # build specific target
868	    if [ -e "${target_path}/targets" ]; then
869	        targets=($(sort -u ${target_path}/targets))
870	        echo targets=${targets[@]}
871	        for target in ${targets[@]}; do
872	            if ! cmake --build ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR} -t $target; then
873	                echo "Error: ############# build ${target} fail ##############"
874	                exit 2
875	            fi
876	            echo -e " $target archive in ${target_path}"
877	        done
878	    fi
879	}

881	# Zsh needs bashcompinit called to support bash-style completion.
882	function enable_zsh_completion() {
883	    # Don't override user's options if bash-style completion is already enabled.
884	    if ! declare -f complete >/dev/null; then
885	        autoload -U compinit && compinit
886	        autoload -U bashcompinit && bashcompinit
887	    fi
888	}

890	function validate_current_shell() {
891	    local current_sh="$(ps -o command -p $$)"
892	    case "$current_sh" in
893	    *bash*)
894	        function check_type() { type -t "$1"; }
895	        ;;
896	    *zsh*)
897	        function check_type() { type "$1"; }
898	        enable_zsh_completion
899	        ;;
900	    *)
901	        echo -e "WARNING: Only bash and zsh are supported.\nUse of other shell would lead to erroneous results."
902	        ;;
903	    esac
904	}

906	# Help generate compile_commands.json to enhance the code jump and lookup efficiency
907	function makefile_bear() {
908	    if [ "${BEAR_MODE:-0}" -eq 0 ]; then
909	        # BEAR command not enabled
910	        "$@"
911	    elif [ "${BEAR_MODE}" -ge 3 ]; then
912	        command bear --append --output "compile_commands.json" -- "$@"
913	    elif [ "${BEAR_MODE}" -ge 2 ]; then
914	        command bear -a -o "compile_commands.json" "$@"
915	    else
916	        # BEAR_MODE not supported
917	        "$@"
918	    fi
919	
920	    return $?
921	}

924	function setup_rust_toolchain() {
925	    local T=$(gettop)
926	    local SYSTEM=$(uname | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
927	
928	    # Set RUST_SRC_PATH to point to rust source library
929	    export RUST_SRC_PATH=$T/prebuilts/rust/${SYSTEM}/nightly/rustc/lib/rustlib/src/rust/library
930	
931	    # Set RUST_UNIFIED_LIB_CONFIG for path-based Rust build configuration
932	    read -r -d '' RUST_UNIFIED_LIB_CONFIG <<EOF
933	[path-bases]
934	runtime = "$T/apps/frameworks/runtimes/rust"
935	external = "$T/apps/external/rust"
936	android = "$T/apps/external/android"
937	EOF
938	    export RUST_UNIFIED_LIB_CONFIG
939	
940	    # Generate .cargo/config.toml at project root
941	    mkdir -p "$T/.cargo"
942	    cat > "$T/.cargo/config.toml" <<< "$RUST_UNIFIED_LIB_CONFIG"
943	
944	    # Set LIBCLANG_PATH for bindgen
945	    export LIBCLANG_PATH=$T/prebuilts/rust/linux/extra_libs
946	    echo "LIBCLANG_PATH set to: $LIBCLANG_PATH"
947	}

949	# Add directories to PATH that are NOT dependent on the lunch target.
950	# For directories that are lunch-specific, add them in set_lunch_paths
951	function setup_global_paths() {
952	    export VELA_ORIGINAL_PS1="$PS1"
953	    export VELA_ORIGINAL_PATH="$PATH"
954	
955	    # wrap bash prompt, mark the current state of vela envs
956	    env_name="vela-env"
957	    PS1="($env_name) $VELA_ORIGINAL_PS1"
958	    export PS1
959	
960	    local T=$(gettop)
961	    if [ ! "$T" ]; then
962	        echo "Couldn't locate the top of the tree.  Try setting TOP."
963	        return
964	    fi
965	
966	    ##################################################################
967	    #                                                                #
968	    #              Read me before you modify this code               #
969	    #                                                                #
970	    #   This function sets VELA_GLOBAL_BUILD_PATHS to what it is  #
971	    #   adding to PATH, and the next time it is run, it removes that #
972	    #   from PATH.  This is required so envsetup.sh can be sourced   #
973	    #   more than once and still have working paths.                 #
974	    #                                                                #
975	    ##################################################################
976	
977	    # Out with the old...
978	    if [ -n "$VELA_GLOBAL_BUILD_PATHS" ]; then
979	        export PATH=${PATH/$VELA_GLOBAL_BUILD_PATHS/}
980	    fi
981	
982	    if [ -n "$VELA_GLOBAL_PYPATHS" ]; then
983	        export PYTHONPATH=${PYTHONPATH/$VELA_GLOBAL_PYPATHS/}
984	    fi
985	
986	    if [ -n "$WASI_SDK_PATH" ]; then
987	        export WASI_SDK_PATH=
988	    fi
989	
990	    if [ -z "$VELA_EXTRA_FLAGS" ]; then
991	        export VELA_EXTRA_FLAGS="-Wno-cpp -Wno-deprecated-declarations -Werror"
992	    fi
993	
994	    if [ -z "$VELA_CMAKE_GENERATOR" ]; then
995	        export VELA_CMAKE_GENERATOR="-GNinja"
996	    fi
997	
998	    SYSTEM=$(uname | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
999	    SYS_ARCH=$(uname -m | sed 's/arm64/aarch64/')
1000	
1001	    ARCH=(
1002	        "xtensa"
1003	        "arm"
1004	        "aarch64"
1005	        "riscv"
1006	        "x86_64"
1007	        "tc32"
1008	        "tricore")
1009	
1010	    TOOLCHAIN=(
1011	        "gcc"
1012	        "clang")
1013	
1014	    if [[ "$XTENSAD_LICENSE_FILE" == "" ]]; then
1015	        export XTENSAD_LICENSE_FILE=28000@10.38.168.2
1016	    fi
1017	    # WASI SDK is clang based toolchain to build WebAssembly targets
1018	    export WASI_SDK_PATH=$T/prebuilts/clang-wasm/${SYSTEM}-${SYS_ARCH}
1019	    # Wasm toolchain is used to optimize wasm binaries
1020	    export WASM_TOOLCHAIN_PATH=$T/prebuilts/clang-wasm/${SYSTEM}-${SYS_ARCH}
1021	    # And in with the new...
1022	    VELA_GLOBAL_BUILD_PATHS=$T
1023	    VELA_GLOBAL_PYPATHS=$T/prebuilts/tools/python/dist-packages/pyelftools
1024	    VELA_GLOBAL_PYPATHS+=:$T/prebuilts/tools/python/dist-packages/cxxfilt
1025	    VELA_GLOBAL_PYPATHS+=:$T/prebuilts/tools/python/dist-packages/Mako
1026	    VELA_GLOBAL_PYPATHS+=:$T/prebuilts/tools/python/dist-packages/ply
1027	    VELA_GLOBAL_PYPATHS+=:$T/prebuilts/tools/python/dist-packages/jsonpath
1028	    VELA_GLOBAL_PYPATHS+=:$T/prebuilts/tools/python/dist-packages/kconfiglib
1029	    VELA_GLOBAL_PYPATHS+=:$T/prebuilts/tools/python/dist-packages/construct
1030	
1031	    # Recommended to use kconfiglib instead of kconfig-frontends
1032	    VELA_GLOBAL_BUILD_PATHS+=:$T/prebuilts/tools/python/bin
1033	
1034	    # gcc
1035	    for ((i = 0; i < ${#ARCH[*]}; i++)); do
1036	        # TODO: remove and change to x86_64-none-elf
1037	        if [ -d $T/prebuilts/gcc/${SYSTEM}-${SYS_ARCH}/${ARCH[@]:$i:1}-none-linux-gnu/bin ]; then
1038	            VELA_GLOBAL_BUILD_PATHS+=:$T/prebuilts/gcc/${SYSTEM}-${SYS_ARCH}/${ARCH[@]:$i:1}-none-linux-gnu/bin
1039	        fi
1040	        for TOOLCHAIN_BIN in $T/prebuilts/gcc/${SYSTEM}-${SYS_ARCH}/${ARCH[@]:$i:1}{,-none}-{eabi,elf}/bin; do
1041	            if [ -d ${TOOLCHAIN_BIN} ]; then
1042	                VELA_GLOBAL_BUILD_PATHS+=:${TOOLCHAIN_BIN}
1043	            fi
1044	        done
1045	    done
1046	
1047	    # TODO: standard clang support for multiple targets
1048	    # clang
1049	
1050	    # clang-arm
1051	    if [ -d $T/prebuilts/clang-arm/${SYSTEM}-${SYS_ARCH}/bin ]; then
1052	        VELA_GLOBAL_BUILD_PATHS+=:$T/prebuilts/clang-arm/${SYSTEM}-${SYS_ARCH}/bin
1053	    fi
1054	    # clang-xtensa
1055	    if [ -d $T/prebuilts/clang-xtensa/${SYSTEM}-${SYS_ARCH}/bin ]; then
1056	        VELA_GLOBAL_BUILD_PATHS+=:$T/prebuilts/clang-xtensa/${SYSTEM}-${SYS_ARCH}/bin
1057	    fi
1058	
1059	    # Host build-tools
1060	    if [ -d $T/prebuilts/build-tools/${SYSTEM}-${SYS_ARCH}/bin ]; then
1061	        VELA_GLOBAL_BUILD_PATHS+=:$T/prebuilts/build-tools/${SYSTEM}-${SYS_ARCH}/bin
1062	    fi
1063	
1064	    lsb_release_version=$(lsb_release -rs | cut -d '.' -f1)
1065	    # Gdb-multiarch Path
1066	    if [ "$lsb_release_version" -ge 22 ] && [ -d $T/prebuilts/gdb/${SYSTEM}-${SYS_ARCH}/gdb-multiarch/bin ]; then
1067	        VELA_GLOBAL_BUILD_PATHS+=:$T/prebuilts/gdb/${SYSTEM}-${SYS_ARCH}/gdb-multiarch/bin
1068	    fi
1069	    # Arm Compiler
1070	    VELA_GLOBAL_BUILD_PATHS+=:$T/prebuilts/clang/${SYSTEM}/armclang/bin
1071	
1072	    # Rust toolchain
1073	    if [ -d $T/prebuilts/rust/${SYSTEM}/nightly/rustc/bin ]; then
1074	        VELA_GLOBAL_BUILD_PATHS+=:$T/prebuilts/rust/${SYSTEM}/nightly/rustc/bin
1075	    fi
1076	
1077	    if [ ! -n "${ARM_PRODUCT_DEF}" ]; then
1078	        export ARM_PRODUCT_DEF=${ROOTDIR}/prebuilts/clang/${SYSTEM}/armclang/mappings/eval.elmap
1079	    fi
1080	    if [ ! -n "${LM_LICENSE_FILE}" ]; then
1081	        export LM_LICENSE_FILE=${HOME}/.arm/ds/licenses/DS000-EV-31030.lic
1082	    fi
1083	    if [ ! -n "${ARMLMD_LICENSE_FILE}" ]; then
1084	        export ARMLMD_LICENSE_FILE=${HOME}/.arm/ds/licenses/DS000-EV-31030.lic
1085	    fi
1086	
1087	    # Generate compile database file compile_commands.json
1088	    export BEAR_MODE=0
1089	    if type bear >/dev/null 2>&1; then
1090	        # get version of bear
1091	        BEAR_VERSION=$(bear --version | awk '{print $2}' | awk -F. '{printf("%d%03d%03d\n", $1,$2,$3)}')
1092	
1093	        # judge version of bear
1094	        if [ $BEAR_VERSION -ge 3000000 ]; then
1095	            # bear3 will not compatible with some arch, but we should use cmake.
1096	            export BEAR_MODE=3
1097	            echo -e "Note: currently not support bear 3.0.0+ for some prebuilt toolchain limited."
1098	        elif [ $BEAR_VERSION -ge 2000000 ]; then
1099	            echo -e "Note: bear 2.4.3 in Ubuntu 20.04 works out of box."
1100	            export BEAR_MODE=2
1101	        fi
1102	    fi
1103	
1104	    # Add prebuilt tool
1105	    VELA_GLOBAL_BUILD_PATHS+=:$T/prebuilts/tools/${SYSTEM}/${SYS_ARCH}
1106	
1107	    # Add CMake prebuilt
1108	    VELA_GLOBAL_BUILD_PATHS+=:$T/prebuilts/tools/cmake/bin
1109	    VELA_GLOBAL_BUILD_PATHS+=:$T/prebuilts/tools/ninja/bin
1110	
1111	    # Additional prebuilt GNU tools
1112	    if [[ ${SYSTEM} == "darwin" ]]; then
1113	        VELA_GLOBAL_BUILD_PATHS+=:$T/prebuilts/tools/gnu/${SYSTEM}/${SYS_ARCH}
1114	        VELA_GLOBAL_BUILD_PATHS+=:$T/prebuilts/tools/gnu/${SYSTEM}/universal
1115	    fi
1116	
1117	    # CCACHE strategy
1118	    export CCACHE_BASEDIR=$T
1119	    export CCACHE_COMPILERCHECK="content"
1120	    export CCACHE_NOHASHDIR=1
1121	    export CCACHE_SLOPPINESS="file_macro,time_macros,include_file_ctime,include_file_mtime"
1122	
1123	    # Finally, set PATH
1124	    export PATH=$VELA_GLOBAL_BUILD_PATHS:$PATH
1125	    export PYTHONPATH=$VELA_GLOBAL_PYPATHS:$PYTHONPATH
1126	}

1128	function vela_env_pack_check() {
1129	    # Skip environment by `export VELA_CHECKENV_SKIP=1` and reset by `unset VELA_CHECKENV_SKIP`
1130	    if [ -n "${VELA_CHECKENV_SKIP}" ] && [ "${VELA_CHECKENV_SKIP}" != "0" ]; then
1131	        echo "Skipping environment check due to VELA_CHECKENV_SKIP=${VELA_CHECKENV_SKIP}"
1132	        return 0
1133	    fi
1134	
1135	    PACKAGES=(
1136	        "autoconf"
1137	        "automake"
1138	        "bison"
1139	        "build-essential"
1140	        "dfu-util"
1141	        "genromfs"
1142	        "flex"
1143	        "git"
1144	        "gperf"
1145	        "libncurses5"
1146	        "lib32ncurses5-dev"
1147	        "libc6-dev-i386"
1148	        "libx11-dev"
1149	        "libx11-dev:i386"
1150	        "libxext-dev"
1151	        "libxext-dev:i386"
1152	        "net-tools"
1153	        "pkgconf"
1154	        "unionfs-fuse"
1155	        "zlib1g-dev"
1156	        "kconfig-frontends"
1157	        "g++-11"
1158	        "g++-11-multilib"
1159	        "libpulse-dev:i386"
1160	        "libasound2-dev:i386"
1161	        "libasound2-plugins:i386"
1162	        "libusb-1.0-0-dev"
1163	        "libusb-1.0-0-dev:i386"
1164	        "libv4l-dev"
1165	        "libv4l-dev:i386"
1166	        "libuv1-dev"
1167	        "libmp3lame-dev:i386"
1168	        "libmad0-dev:i386"
1169	        "libv4l-dev:i386"
1170	        "npm"
1171	        "nodejs"
1172	        "xxd"
1173	        "qemu-system-arm"
1174	        "qemu-efi-aarch64"
1175	        "qemu-utils"
1176	        "nasm"
1177	        "yasm"
1178	        "libdivsufsort-dev"
1179	        "libc++abi-dev"
1180	        "libprotobuf-dev"
1181	        "protobuf-compiler"
1182	        "protobuf-c-compiler"
1183	        "gcc-multilib"
1184	        "g++-multilib"
1185	        "gettext"
1186	        "mtools"
1187	    )
1188	    declare -A INSTALLS
1189	    INSTALLED_PKGS=$(dpkg -l | awk '/^ii/ {print $2}')
1190	
1191	    for pkg in "${PACKAGES[@]}"; do
1192	        if ! grep -q "^${pkg}$" <<< "$INSTALLED_PKGS"; then
1193	            echo "WARNING: no packages found matching ${pkg}"
1194	            INSTALLS[${#INSTALLS[@]}]=$pkg

1196	    done
1197	
1198	    if [ ${#INSTALLS[*]} -eq 0 ]; then
1199	        return
1200	    fi
1201	
1202	    if [ ${#INSTALLS[*]} -eq 1 ] && [ "${INSTALLS[0]}" = "kconfig-frontends" ]; then
1203	        return
1204	    fi
1205	
1206	    echo "*************************************************************************************"
1207	    echo "The environment of Vela depends on above tools, Run the following command to install:"
1208	    echo ""
1209	    echo " sudo dpkg --add-architecture i386"
1210	
1211	    for ((i = 0; i < ${#INSTALLS[*]}; i++)); do
1212	        result=$(apt-cache search ${INSTALLS[$i]})
1213	        if [ "$result" = "" ]; then
1214	            if [ "${INSTALLS[$i]}" = "kconfig-frontends" ]; then
1215	                unset INSTALLS[$i]
1216	            fi
1217	        fi
1218	    done
1219	
1220	    echo " sudo apt-get install -y software-properties-common"
1221	    echo " sudo add-apt-repository ppa:ubuntu-toolchain-r/test"
1222	    echo " sudo apt-get update"
1223	    echo " sudo apt-get install -y ${INSTALLS[@]}"
1224	    echo ""
1225	    echo "*************************************************************************************"
1226	}

1228	# Execute the contents of any vendorsetup.sh files we can find.
1229	# Unless we find an allowed-vendorsetup_sh-files file, in which case we'll only
1230	# load those.
1231	#
1232	# This allows loading only approved vendorsetup.sh files
1233	function source_vendorsetup() {
1234	    unset VENDOR_PYTHONPATH
1235	    local T="$(gettop)"
1236	    allowed=
1237	    for f in $(cd "$T" && find -L vendor -maxdepth 6 -name 'allowed-vendorsetup_sh-files' 2>/dev/null | sort); do
1238	        if [ -n "$allowed" ]; then
1239	            echo "More than one 'allowed_vendorsetup_sh-files' file found, not including any vendorsetup.sh files:"
1240	            echo "  $allowed"
1241	            echo "  $f"
1242	            return
1243	        fi
1244	        allowed="$T/$f"
1245	    done
1246	
1247	    allowed_files=
1248	    [ -n "$allowed" ] && allowed_files=$(cat "$allowed")
1249	    for dir in vendor; do
1250	        for f in $(cd "$T" && test -d $dir &&
1251	            find -L $dir -maxdepth 6 -name 'vendorsetup.sh' 2>/dev/null | sort); do
1252	
1253	            if [[ -z "$allowed" || "$allowed_files" =~ $f ]]; then
1254	                echo "including $f"
1255	                . "$T/$f"
1256	            else
1257	                echo "ignoring $f, not in $allowed"
1258	            fi
1259	        done
1260	    done
1261	    # source Top custom vendorsetup.sh if exists
1262	    if [ -e $T/vendorsetup.sh ]; then
1263	        echo "including root custom vendorsetup.sh"
1264	        . "$T/vendorsetup.sh"
1265	    fi
1266	}

## 1. 需要先配置编译环境吗？—— 基本不需要额外安装

openvela 是**自包含构建**，工具链全部预置在 `prebuilts/` 里，检查结果：

| 检查项 | 状态 |
|---|---|
| prebuilt cmake / ninja | ✅ 就位（`prebuilts/tools/cmake`、`ninja`） |
| 交叉编译器 aarch64 / arm / x86_64 gcc | ✅ 就位 |
| build-tools、python 依赖 | ✅ 就位 |
| 宿主机 python3 / git / bash | ✅ 有 |
| 宿主机 make / gcc / cmake | ❌ 无，但**没关系**（`envsetup.sh` 会用 prebuilt 的） |
| CPU / 磁盘 | ✅ 24 核 / 87G 可用 |

所以**不需要 `apt install` 任何东西**。唯一要做的是 `source build/envsetup.sh`，它会自动把 prebuilt 工具链加进 PATH。（`unionfs-fuse` 仅在 `-m` 树外构建模式才需要，默认树内构建不用。）

## 2. 目标硬件平台有哪些

探查到 `vendor/openvela/boards/` 下有三个 board，各自有多个 config：

- **vela**（通用平台，最全）：`qemu-arm64-v8a-ap`、`qemu-armeabi-v7a-ap`、`qemu-x86_64-ap`、`goldfish-*`（Android 模拟器）等 12 个
- **smartspeaker**（智能音箱真实硬件）：`smartspeaker`、`smartspeaker-arm64`、`smartspeaker-knsh`
- **sil**（SiL 芯片）：`sil_arm32r_nsh_bl` 等 4 个

默认 lunch 菜单注册的是 `goldfish-armeabi-v7a-ap` 和 `smartspeaker` 系列。

## 3. 具体编译步骤（以标准流程为例）

```bash
cd /mnt/e/openvela
source build/envsetup.sh      # ① 配置环境（必须，每次新 shell 都要）
lunch <vendor>-<board>-<config>   # ② 选择目标平台
m -j$(nproc)                  # ③ 编译（默认 CMake+Ninja）
```

产物输出到 `out/<vendor>_<board>_<config>/`，可用 `emulator.sh <产物目录>` 启动模拟器。

# Update Config Skill

Modify Claude Code configuration by updating settings.json files.

## When Hooks Are Required (Not Memory)

If the user wants something to happen automatically in response to an EVENT, they need a **hook** configured in settings.json. Memory/preferences cannot trigger automated actions.

**These require hooks:**
- "Before compacting, ask me what to preserve" → PreCompact hook
- "After writing files, run prettier" → PostToolUse hook with Write|Edit matcher
- "When I run bash commands, log them" → PreToolUse hook with Bash matcher
- "Always run tests after code changes" → PostToolUse hook

**Hook events:** PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PostCompact, Stop, Notification, SessionStart

## CRITICAL: Read Before Write

**Always read the existing settings file before making changes.** Merge new settings with existing ones - never replace the entire file.

## CRITICAL: Use AskUserQuestion for Ambiguity

When the user's request is ambiguous, use AskUserQuestion to clarify:
- Which settings file to modify (user/project/local)
- Whether to add to existing arrays or replace them
- Specific values when multiple options exist

## Decision: /config command vs Direct Edit

**Suggest the `/config` slash command** for these simple settings:
- `theme`, `editorMode`, `verbose`, `model`
- `language`, `alwaysThinkingEnabled`
- `permissions.defaultMode`

**Edit settings.json directly** for:
- Hooks (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, etc.)
- Complex permission rules (allow/deny arrays)
- Environment variables
- MCP server configuration
- Plugin configuration

## Workflow

1. **Clarify intent** - Ask if the request is ambiguous
2. **Read existing file** - Use Read tool on the target settings file
3. **Merge carefully** - Preserve existing settings, especially arrays
4. **Edit file** - Use Edit tool (if file doesn't exist, ask user to create it first)
5. **Confirm** - Tell user what was changed

## Merging Arrays (Important!)

When adding to permission arrays or hook arrays, **merge with existing**, don't replace:

**WRONG** (replaces existing permissions):
```json
{ "permissions": { "allow": ["Bash(npm *)"] } }
```

**RIGHT** (preserves existing + adds new):
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "Bash(git *)",      // existing
      "Edit(.claude)",    // existing
      "Bash(npm *)"       // new
    ]
  }
}
```

## Settings File Locations

Choose the appropriate file based on scope:

| File | Scope | Git | Use For |
|------|-------|-----|---------|
| `~/.claude/settings.json` | Global | N/A | Personal preferences for all projects |
| `.claude/settings.json` | Project | Commit | Team-wide hooks, permissions, plugins |
| `.claude/settings.local.json` | Project | Gitignore | Personal overrides for this project |

Settings load in order: user → project → local (later overrides earlier).

## Settings Schema Reference

### Permissions
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": ["Bash(npm *)", "Edit(.claude)", "Read"],
    "deny": ["Bash(rm -rf *)"],
    "ask": ["Write(/etc/*)"],
    "defaultMode": "default" | "plan" | "acceptEdits" | "dontAsk",
    "additionalDirectories": ["/extra/dir"]
  }
}
```

**Permission Rule Syntax:**
- Exact match: `"Bash(npm run test)"`
- Prefix wildcard: `"Bash(git *)"` - matches `git`, `git status`, `git commit`, etc.
- Tool only: `"Read"` - allows all Read operations

### Environment Variables
```json
{
  "env": {
    "DEBUG": "true",
    "MY_API_KEY": "value"
  }
}
```

### Model & Agent
```json
{
  "model": "sonnet",  // or "fable", "opus", "haiku", full model ID
  "agent": "agent-name",
  "alwaysThinkingEnabled": true
}
```

### Attribution (Commits & PRs)
```json
{
  "attribution": {
    "commit": "Custom commit trailer text",
    "pr": "Custom PR description text"
  }
}
```
Set `commit` or `pr` to empty string `""` to hide that attribution.

### MCP Server Management
```json
{
  "enableAllProjectMcpServers": true,
  "enabledMcpjsonServers": ["server1", "server2"],
  "disabledMcpjsonServers": ["blocked-server"]
}
```

### Plugins
```json
{
  "enabledPlugins": {
    "formatter@anthropic-tools": true
  }
}
```
Plugin syntax: `plugin-name@source` where source is `claude-code-marketplace`, `claude-plugins-official`, or `builtin`.

### Other Settings
- `language`: Preferred response language (e.g., "japanese")
- `cleanupPeriodDays`: Days to keep transcripts before automatic cleanup (default: 30; minimum 1)
- `respectGitignore`: Whether to respect .gitignore (default: true)
- `spinnerTipsEnabled`: Show tips in spinner
- `spinnerVerbs`: Customize spinner verbs (`{ "mode": "append" | "replace", "verbs": [...] }`)
- `spinnerTipsOverride`: Override spinner tips (`{ "excludeDefault": true, "tips": ["Custom tip"] }`)
- `syntaxHighlightingDisabled`: Disable diff highlighting


## Hooks Configuration

Hooks run commands at specific points in Claude Code's lifecycle.

### Hook Structure
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "EVENT_NAME": [
      {
        "matcher": "ToolName|OtherTool",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "your-command-here",
            "timeout": 60,
            "statusMessage": "Running..."
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Hook Events

| Event | Matcher | Purpose |
|-------|---------|---------|
| PermissionRequest | Tool name | Run before permission prompt |
| PreToolUse | Tool name | Run before tool, can block |
| PostToolUse | Tool name | Run after successful tool |
| PostToolUseFailure | Tool name | Run after tool fails |
| Notification | Notification type | Run on notifications |
| Stop | - | Run when Claude stops (including clear, resume, compact) |
| PreCompact | "manual"/"auto" | Before compaction |
| PostCompact | "manual"/"auto" | After compaction (receives summary) |
| UserPromptSubmit | - | When user submits |
| SessionStart | - | When session starts |

**Common tool matchers:** `Bash`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`

### Hook Types

**1. Command Hook** - Runs a shell command:
```json
{ "type": "command", "command": "prettier --write $FILE", "timeout": 30 }
```

**2. Prompt Hook** - Evaluates a condition with LLM:
```json
{ "type": "prompt", "prompt": "Is this safe? $ARGUMENTS" }
```
Only available for tool events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest.

**3. Agent Hook** - Runs an agent with tools:
```json
{ "type": "agent", "prompt": "Verify tests pass: $ARGUMENTS" }
```
Only available for tool events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest.

### Hook Input (stdin JSON)
```json
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "tool_name": "Write",
  "tool_input": { "file_path": "/path/to/file.txt", "content": "..." },
  "tool_response": { "success": true }  // PostToolUse only
}
```

### Hook JSON Output

Hooks can return JSON to control behavior:

```json
{
  "systemMessage": "Warning shown to user in UI",
  "continue": false,
  "stopReason": "Message shown when blocking",
  "suppressOutput": false,
  "decision": "block",
  "reason": "Explanation for decision",
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PostToolUse",
    "additionalContext": "Context injected back to model"
  }
}
```

**Fields:**
- `systemMessage` - Display a message to the user (all hooks)
- `continue` - Set to `false` to block/stop (default: true)
- `stopReason` - Message shown when `continue` is false
- `suppressOutput` - Hide stdout from transcript (default: false)
- `decision` - "block" for PostToolUse/Stop/UserPromptSubmit hooks (deprecated for PreToolUse, use hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision instead)
- `reason` - Explanation for decision
- `hookSpecificOutput` - Event-specific output (must include `hookEventName`):
  - `additionalContext` - Text injected into model context
  - `permissionDecision` - "allow", "deny", or "ask" (PreToolUse only)
  - `permissionDecisionReason` - Reason for the permission decision (PreToolUse only)
  - `updatedInput` - Modified tool input (PreToolUse only)

### Common Patterns

**Auto-format after writes:**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_response.filePath // .tool_input.file_path' | { read -r f; prettier --write \"$f\"; } 2>/dev/null || true"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

**Log all bash commands:**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Bash",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_input.command' >> ~/.claude/bash-log.txt"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

**Stop hook that displays message to user:**

Command must output JSON with `systemMessage` field:
```bash
# Example command that outputs: {"systemMessage": "Session complete!"}
echo '{"systemMessage": "Session complete!"}'
```

**Run tests after code changes:**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // .tool_response.filePath' | grep -E '\\.(ts|js)$' && npm test || true"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```


## Constructing a Hook (with verification)

Given an event, matcher, target file, and desired behavior, follow this flow. Each step catches a different failure class — a hook that silently does nothing is worse than no hook.

1. **Dedup check.** Read the target file. If a hook already exists on the same event+matcher, show the existing command and ask: keep it, replace it, or add alongside.

2. **Construct the command for THIS project — don't assume.** The hook receives JSON on stdin. Build a command that:
   - Extracts any needed payload safely — use `jq -r` into a quoted variable or `{ read -r f; ... "$f"; }`, NOT unquoted `| xargs` (splits on spaces)
   - Invokes the underlying tool the way this project runs it (npx/bunx/yarn/pnpm? Makefile target? globally-installed?)
   - Skips inputs the tool doesn't handle (formatters often have `--ignore-unknown`; if not, guard by extension)
   - Stays RAW for now — no `|| true`, no stderr suppression. You'll wrap it after the pipe-test passes.

3. **Pipe-test the raw command.** Synthesize the stdin payload the hook will receive and pipe it directly:
   - `Pre|PostToolUse` on `Write|Edit`: `echo '{"tool_name":"Edit","tool_input":{"file_path":"<a real file from this repo>"}}' | <cmd>`
   - `Pre|PostToolUse` on `Bash`: `echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"ls"}}' | <cmd>`
   - `Stop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`SessionStart`: most commands don't read stdin, so `echo '{}' | <cmd>` suffices

   Check exit code AND side effect (file actually formatted, test actually ran). If it fails you get a real error — fix (wrong package manager? tool not installed? jq path wrong?) and retest. Once it works, wrap with `2>/dev/null || true` (unless the user wants a blocking check).

4. **Write the JSON.** Merge into the target file (schema shape in the "Hook Structure" section above). If this creates `.claude/settings.local.json` for the first time, add it to .gitignore — the Write tool doesn't auto-gitignore it.

5. **Validate syntax + schema in one shot:**

   `jq -e '.hooks.<event>[] | select(.matcher == "<matcher>") | .hooks[] | select(.type == "command") | .command' <target-file>`

   Exit 0 + prints your command = correct. Exit 4 = matcher doesn't match. Exit 5 = malformed JSON or wrong nesting. A broken settings.json silently disables ALL settings from that file — fix any pre-existing malformation too.

6. **Prove the hook fires** — only for `Pre|PostToolUse` on a matcher you can trigger in-turn (`Write|Edit` via Edit, `Bash` via Bash). `Stop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`SessionStart` fire outside this turn — skip to step 7.

   For a **formatter** on `PostToolUse`/`Write|Edit`: introduce a detectable violation via Edit (two consecutive blank lines, bad indentation, missing semicolon — something this formatter corrects; NOT trailing whitespace, Edit strips that before writing), re-read, confirm the hook **fixed** it. For **anything else**: temporarily prefix the command in settings.json with `echo "$(date) hook fired" >> /tmp/claude-hook-check.txt; `, trigger the matching tool (Edit for `Write|Edit`, a harmless `true` for `Bash`), read the sentinel file.

   **Always clean up** — revert the violation, strip the sentinel prefix — whether the proof passed or failed.

   **If proof fails but pipe-test passed and `jq -e` passed**: the settings watcher isn't watching `.claude/` — it only watches directories that had a settings file when this session started. The hook is written correctly. Tell the user to open `/hooks` once (reloads config) or restart — you can't do this yourself; `/hooks` is a user UI menu and opening it ends this turn.

7. **Handoff.** Tell the user the hook is live (or needs `/hooks`/restart per the watcher caveat). Point them at `/hooks` to review, edit, or disable it later. The UI only shows "Ran N hooks" if a hook errors or is slow — silent success is invisible by design.


## Example Workflows

### Adding a Hook

User: "Format my code after Claude writes it"

1. **Clarify**: Which formatter? (prettier, gofmt, etc.)
2. **Read**: `.claude/settings.json` (or create if missing)
3. **Merge**: Add to existing hooks, don't replace
4. **Result**:
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "jq -r '.tool_response.filePath // .tool_input.file_path' | { read -r f; prettier --write \"$f\"; } 2>/dev/null || true"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

### Adding Permissions

User: "Allow npm commands without prompting"

1. **Read**: Existing permissions
2. **Merge**: Add `Bash(npm *)` to allow array
3. **Result**: Combined with existing allows

### Environment Variables

User: "Set DEBUG=true"

1. **Decide**: User settings (global) or project settings?
2. **Read**: Target file
3. **Merge**: Add to env object
```json
{ "env": { "DEBUG": "true" } }
```

## Common Mistakes to Avoid

1. **Replacing instead of merging** - Always preserve existing settings
2. **Wrong file** - Ask user if scope is unclear
3. **Invalid JSON** - Validate syntax after changes
4. **Forgetting to read first** - Always read before write

## Troubleshooting Hooks

If a hook isn't running:
1. **Check the settings file** - Read ~/.claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.json
2. **Verify JSON syntax** - Invalid JSON silently fails
3. **Check the matcher** - Does it match the tool name? (e.g., "Bash", "Write", "Edit")
4. **Check hook type** - Is it "command", "prompt", or "agent"?
5. **Test the command** - Run the hook command manually to see if it works
6. **Use --debug** - Run `claude --debug` to see hook execution logs

        },
        "timeoutMs": {

          "minimum": 1000,

        },

            {

      "description": "Whether file picker should respect .gitignore files (default: true). Note: .ignore files are always respected.",
      "type": "boolean"

          "type": "boolean"

          "description": "Minutes of inactivity that count as a break and reset the timer (default 15)",
          "type": "integer",
          "exclusiveMinimum": 0,
          "maximum": 9007199254740991
        },
        "message": {
          "description": "Custom reminder text. Leave unset for a rotating set of friendly nudges.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      }
    },
    "quietHours": {
      "description": "@internal Opt-in quiet hours. When enabled, shows a single soft nudge per session while inside the configured local-time window. Never blocks.",
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "enabled": {
          "description": "Show a one-time nudge when you start or keep using the CLI inside your quiet-hours window (default false).",
          "type": "boolean"

          "pattern": "^([01]?\\d|2[0-3]):[0-5]\\d$"
        },
        "end": {
          "description": "End of the quiet-hours window, 24-hour local time \"HH:MM\". May be earlier than start for an overnight range.",
          "type": "string",
          "pattern": "^([01]?\\d|2[0-3]):[0-5]\\d$"
        }
      }
    },
    "cleanupPeriodDays": {
      "description": "Number of days to retain chat transcripts before automatic cleanup (default: 30). Minimum 1. Use a large value for long retention; use --no-session-persistence to disable transcript writes entirely.",
      "type": "integer",
      "exclusiveMinimum": 0,
      "maximum": 9007199254740991
    },
    "skillListingMaxDescChars": {
